direct_ppas.notes: Restart of TMI Unit 1, first commercial US nuclear plant to reopen after shutdown.
Expanded agreement with Constellation covering multiple nuclear plants.

data.name: Brandaleone Lab for Data and Visualization
xAI Colossus Supercluster
data.notes: Elon Musk's AI company launched Phase 1 (100K Nvidia H100s) in September 2024 in a repurposed Memphis factory. Phase 2 targets 1M H100-equivalent GPUs at ~960 MW — making it the largest AI training cluster in the world by compute. Drawing power from the MISO grid, the site has triggered grid reliability concerns for Tennessee.

data.name: Microsoft AI Campus — Racine County
data.notes: Announced January 2023 as part of Microsoft's $3.3B Wisconsin investment. 315-acre campus near Caledonia targeting AI workloads. We Energies must build new gas peaker plants to supply the load — drawing criticism from state environmental regulators. Expected to be one of the largest data center campuses in the Midwest.

data.name: Microsoft AI Campus — Mt. Pleasant
data.notes: Second Microsoft campus in the Milwaukee metro, sited on the former Foxconn factory land that was acquired by Racine County. Part of the same $3.3B Wisconsin commitment. Construction began 2024.

data.name: Microsoft Data Center — Cheyenne
data.notes: Announced 2023. Wyoming's low-cost power and favorable tax environment attracted Microsoft. The site is positioned to take advantage of Wyoming's significant wind energy build-out and proximity to Colorado's fiber backbone.

data.name: Microsoft Azure Campus — Goodyear
data.notes: Major AI-optimized campus west of Phoenix, part of Microsoft's 2024 Arizona expansion announcement. APS grid (~30% nuclear from Palo Verde, ~40% gas) serves the site. Water-intensive evaporative cooling in one of the driest metros in the US has drawn scrutiny from Maricopa County water planners.

data.name: Google Nuclear SMR Campus — Hamlin Township

direct_ppas.notes: First commercial nuclear SMR offtake agreement; 6-7 reactors planned online 2030-2035

data.notes: In October 2023 Google signed the world's first commercial nuclear SMR power purchase agreement with Kairos Power to supply 500 MW from its fluoride salt-cooled High Temperature Reactor (FHR). First reactors are targeted for 2030, with full deployment by 2035. This is a landmark deal for the nuclear SMR industry — Google is using it to power a future campus in northeastern Pennsylvania.

data.name: Google Cloud Region — Bridgeport
data.notes: Announced 2023 as part of Google's $200M West Virginia investment. Bridgeport site was chosen for its access to Appalachian Power's grid and proximity to fiber routes. West Virginia's grid is still ~75% coal-powered — a challenge for Google's carbon-free energy commitments.

data.name: Google Data Center — Virginia Beach
data.notes: Sited to serve as a submarine cable landing point for Google's transatlantic and transpacific fiber. Virginia Beach is the landing point for multiple subsea cables (Dunant, Grace Hopper). Announced 2024 as part of Google's $1B Virginia investment. Dominion Energy offshore wind farm nearby is expected to partially power the campus.

data.name: Amazon AWS Nuclear Campus — Berwick

direct_ppas.notes: Direct nuclear power purchase — AWS co-located campus on Susquehanna nuclear plant property

data.notes: Amazon signed a $650M agreement in 2023 to acquire Talen Energy's data center campus co-located on the 2,500 MW Susquehanna nuclear plant. The deal — the largest nuclear-powered data center acquisition in history — was initially blocked by FERC in May 2024 over grid reliability concerns, then renegotiated with capacity limits. This campus represents a new paradigm: directly co-locating AI compute with nuclear generation.

data.name: Amazon AWS Campus — Prince William County
data.notes: Major AWS expansion in the Gainesville/Manassas corridor of Northern Virginia, adding to Amazon's already dominant position in the region. Part of a multi-year, multi-billion dollar AWS buildout in the DC metro. Prince William County has become a secondary data center hub as Loudoun County runs out of substation capacity.

data.name: Meta AI Campus — Huntsville
data.notes: Announced 2024 as part of Meta's $800M Alabama investment. Designed to train Meta's Llama AI models at scale. Huntsville was chosen for low electricity costs (TVA-served grid), available land, and Alabama's data center tax incentives. The campus will train the next generation of Meta's large language models.

data.name: Meta AI Data Center — DeKalb
data.notes: Part of Meta's 2024 Midwest expansion, complementing its existing Sandwich, IL facility. ComEd's grid in northern Illinois is ~55% nuclear, making this one of Meta's lower-carbon campuses. Designed for AI inference workloads at scale.

data.name: Meta AI Campus — Temple
data.notes: Announced 2024 as Meta's major ERCOT-grid campus for AI training. Central Texas location provides access to abundant West Texas wind power via ERCOT's transmission system. Temple's economic development incentives and land costs made it competitive with DFW and Austin suburbs.

data.name: CoreWeave GPU Supercluster — Muskogee
data.notes: Announced 2024 as potentially the world's largest single data center campus at 1+ GW planned capacity. CoreWeave — the GPU cloud provider backed by Nvidia and valued at $19B after its 2024 IPO — is building AI training infrastructure for Microsoft, OpenAI, and other top AI labs. Oklahoma's low power costs and SPP grid access to wind energy made it competitive with Texas.

data.name: Stargate / OpenAI — Abilene
data.notes: The first campus of the Stargate Project — a $500B AI infrastructure joint venture between OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle announced January 2025. Construction began immediately in Abilene with $11B committed to this site. When complete, it will be the most powerful AI supercomputer facility ever built. ERCOT grid concerns: Abilene sits on AEP's Texas network, and 1.2 GW of new load will require major transmission upgrades. West Texas wind and solar are expected to provide significant renewable supply.

data.name: Google Cloud Expansion — Licking County
data.notes: Google has been the anchor tenant in New Albany, Ohio since 2006 and is expanding its campus to 500 MW+ as part of a $1B+ Ohio investment announced 2024. The PJM grid in Ohio (~30% nuclear from FirstEnergy plants) provides relatively low-carbon power. This expansion includes AI training infrastructure for Google DeepMind and Google Cloud.

data.name: Apple Data Center — Waukee Expansion
data.notes: Apple is expanding its existing Waukee, Iowa campus — its first purpose-built data center — as part of a $430M Iowa investment. MidAmerican Energy's grid is ~60-70% wind-powered, making this one of Apple's cleanest campuses. The expansion adds AI inference capacity for Apple Intelligence features.

data.name: CoreWeave Compute Campus — Blue Bell
data.notes: CoreWeave's East Coast AI compute hub near Philadelphia, chosen for proximity to financial and pharma customers in the Mid-Atlantic. PECO's high nuclear mix (~50%, primarily from Limerick and Peach Bottom plants) aligns with CoreWeave's sustainability commitments. Built to serve Microsoft Azure AI and scientific computing customers.

data.name: Amazon AWS Clarksburg Campus
data.notes: AWS's northernmost Maryland campus, serving US government and financial sector customers in the DC corridor. Located in Montgomery County to serve the Maryland Tech Corridor. Pepco's grid is primarily nuclear and gas. The site sits within the PJM interconnection, giving AWS access to the largest competitive electricity market in the world.

data.name: Microsoft AI Infrastructure — Redmond Expansion
data.notes: Microsoft's ongoing expansion of its Redmond/Eastside campus AI infrastructure, co-located with its HQ. PSE grid provides significant hydro (BPA contracts) and wind. Designed to run OpenAI's research models at Microsoft's headquarters — Azure's primary AI R&D campus. Expansion triggered by the OpenAI partnership and the explosive demand for GPT-4 and Copilot workloads.
